sections.html:
Oxford is the Lafayette County seat in north Mississippi, about 75 miles south-southeast of Memphis, and it is built around the University of Mississippi, known as Ole Miss. The 2020 census population was 25,416. Highway 6, which also carries U.S. 278, runs west to Batesville and east to Pontotoc. Highway 7 runs north to Holly Springs and south to Water Valley, and Highway 30 heads northeast toward New Albany.

The city sits in the North Central Hills, a region of forested ridges and red clay. Downtown rests on one ridge and the campus on another, with the main commercial corridors in the valleys between. On a sloped lot with red clay, check drainage and grading before you list, because water problems are easy for a buyer to spot.

sections.h2: How Ole Miss shapes the housing market
sections.html:
The university is the biggest single influence on Oxford housing, and it makes the city's numbers look different from the rest of north Mississippi. Fall 2026 enrollment reached 28,960 across all campuses, a 2 percent increase and a fourth straight record, and the first-time freshman class of 5,363 was the third largest ever. Rentals and investor-owned houses make up a notable share of the market as a result.

Student-market measureOxford, 2020 census
Median age27.8 years
Households11,856
One-person households43.8%
Housing units15,944 (25.6% vacant)
Homeowner vacancy rate2.9%
Rental vacancy rate19.7%

Only 19.8 percent of households include children under 18. Both vacancy figures are high for a city this size, so a landlord should compare lease end dates with the target closing date before choosing a sale route.

  • Owner-occupants selling a family home usually follow a normal listing path.
  • Landlords with student tenants should review lease end dates before setting a closing date.
  • Heirs of a house that needs work may prefer a quick as-is sale.

Oxford publishes Historic Design Guidelines for its older areas. Owners of houses in historic areas should read them before making exterior changes, and should tell a buyer about any approvals that were granted. The campus itself, called University, Mississippi, is unincorporated territory that the city of Oxford surrounds completely, so it is worth confirming which side of a boundary your address falls on when a question about services comes up.

The Building division administers the building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and fuel gas codes and the erosion control ordinances. It accepts residential and commercial permit applications, performs inspections and issues certificates of occupancy or completion. Permit applications and inspection scheduling are moving to an online system called EnerGov.

City codes currently include the 2024 International Building Code, the 2024 International Residential Code with local changes, the 2023 National Electrical Code, and the 2024 plumbing, mechanical, fuel gas and fire codes. A building permit fee schedule and a 2026 permit fee chart are published too.

If you renovated without a permit, a buyer's inspector may ask for the file. On a hilly lot, read the erosion control ordinance, since grading and clearing can trigger requirements. A cash buyer will often take a house with open permit questions, but you should still disclose what you know. Details are on the City of Oxford Building and Development page, and all ordinances are on Municode.

sections.h2: Lafayette County property tax and homestead
sections.html:
The tax is due by February 1 each year. You can pay at the office, by phone or online, and card payments carry a 2.35 percent fee. Mississippi assesses an owner-occupied single-family home at 10 percent of true value and other real property at 15 percent, so a rental is taxed on a larger share of its value than an owner's home.

Real property must be revalued at least every four years. An owner who disagrees can request a hearing before the Board of Supervisors, usually by the first Monday in August. A house inside Oxford pays a county rate, a school district rate and a city rate. January 1 is the assessment date, so the owner of record on that day gets the bill, and your closing agent will normally split the year between you and the buyer.

Homestead exemption applications go to the tax assessor between January 1 and April 1. A change in ownership or occupancy can require a new application, which matters when a student-area house goes from rental to owner-occupied. Unpaid taxes can end in a county tax sale, so pay or arrange a payoff before closing.

Two public school districts cover Oxford: the Oxford School District serves most of the city, and the Lafayette County School District serves small outlying sections. Buyers with children ask about this first, so confirm which district your address is in. The city also runs a bus service, Oxford-University Transit, and students and faculty ride free with university identification.

sections.h2: Your options for selling in Oxford
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell privately or accept a cash offer. Because the university shapes the market, the best path depends on who owns the house and what shape it is in. A renovated home near campus may draw interest through a listing, while an inherited house with deferred repairs may fit a cash sale better.

Most sellers must deliver a written property condition disclosure statement before title transfers (Mississippi Code section 89-1-503). A buyer who receives it late has three days after in-person delivery, or five after mailing, to cancel the offer.

We buy houses in Oxford as is, with no commission and no closing costs to you. Send us the address and we will explain how a cash offer works and what timeline fits. If the offer does not suit you, you owe nothing.

Cash buyers often purchase rentals as is. Check your lease end dates and your tenants' rights before choosing a closing date, and hand the buyer the leases and rent records. A student house that sits empty between terms still costs taxes, insurance and utilities, so a sale timed to a lease end can save money.

faqs.q: How far is Oxford, MS from Memphis?
faqs.a: About 75 miles south-southeast of Memphis, Tennessee. Highway 6 and Highway 7 are the main routes into the city.

faqs.q: How many students attend Ole Miss?
faqs.a: The University of Mississippi reported 28,960 students across all campuses in fall 2026, a 2 percent increase and its fourth straight enrollment record.

faqs.q: When are Lafayette County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By February 1 each year. You can pay at the tax collector's office, by phone or online, and card payments carry a 2.35 percent fee.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for renovations in Oxford, MS?
faqs.a: The Building division issues residential and commercial permits and performs inspections. Contact the city to confirm whether your project needs one.

faqs.q: Can I sell a student rental in Oxford for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers often purchase rentals as is. Check your lease end dates and the tenants' rights before choosing a closing date.
